title: Slip Coding.pdf — page 21
text:
Sublimits
Sublimits give lower limits for certain perils, regions, occupancies, or specific locations.
• Example: California EQ may have a lower limit than EQ in other states.
If the sublimit is higher than (policy limit + excess), then we don’t need to capture it.
If the sublimit applies to the entire peril (e.g., all Flood) or to all locations in that region (e.g., all CA properties for CA EQ), then enter it as 
a blanket limit in the P ARTOF column.
If the sublimit is very specific (only some regions/occupancies/addresses), it must be added later using RiskLink Special Conditions.
Not all sublimits can be modelled. Avoid things like boiler damage. Only capture:
• Nat Cat perils (EQ, Flood, Wind, etc.)
• Defined regions/countries. See the Zone and Tier Definitions folder in the inhouse guides folder documentation defining common 
peril regions
• Defined occupancies (schools, warehouses, etc.)
• Vehicles or fine art only if they represent 100% of the value at that location
• Specific addresses/locations clearly mentioned
